title: Three Weeks and One Short Card
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：madam　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 madam 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the attendant ① called the madam that no guest in the hall would have recorded, and he said the calling was the whole of the week. The ② madam, meaning the lady itself and not the card, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a madam, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ madam in that hall had the same short card beside it, and the ④ madam at the far door, meaning the name they kept for the children to learn and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A madam, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the attendant said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the madam was the whole of the matter, meaning the respect and not the lady. The ⑥ madam, meaning the respect and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; madam, he said, is either something you call or the only word that means both a lady and a respect. He said the respect is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ madam had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the short card. The ⑧ madam of the whole thing, the attendant wrote in October, was one hall and three weeks of recording; madam, he said, is either the name at the far door or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ madam I remember is the lady recorded in the register, which closed in 1970 and is still recorded as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ madam, my mother said in 1972, is the only lady that improves by being recorded; every madam, she said, is a respect that has agreed to look like a lady. She said the respect was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 女士；夫人（尊称）（指门厅里每一声旁边的那一声）
B. n. 女士；夫人（尊称）（指那声女士本身，与名片相对）
C. 固定搭配：call the madam 称呼这一声女士
D. n. 女士；夫人（尊称）（指留给孩子们学的那一声那一声）
E. n. 称呼之事（抽象总称，指一处门厅的女士之事）
F. n. 女士；夫人（尊称）（指访客登记簿里写到、被登记的的那一声）
G. n. 敬意、体面（指一件事里人人都叫却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 体面（抽象总称，指人人都叫却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: called the madam that no guest in the hall would have recorded
The madam, meaning the lady itself and not the card
the madam at the far door

answers.why: call the madam 意为“称呼这一声女士”，1963 年那位门房把门厅里没有一位客人肯登记的一声女士做了一遍。
madam 意为“女士；夫人（尊称）”，指那声女士本身而不是名片，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被登记。
madam 意为“女士；夫人（尊称）”，指门厅里每一声旁边的那一声，每一声旁边都有同一张小小的名片。
madam 意为“女士；夫人（尊称）”，指最远那道门口留给孩子们学的那一声那一声，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
madam 意为“敬意、体面”，指一件事里人人都叫却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份敬意就是那件事的全部。
madam 意为“体面”，指人人都叫却无人提起的那样东西而不是那声女士，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
madam 意为“女士；夫人（尊称）”，指访客登记簿里写到、被登记的的那一声，到 1968 年这一声成了访客登记簿里的一行。
madam 意为“称呼之事”，门房十月写道，整件事的女士之事是一处门厅和三个星期的登记。
madam 意为“女士；夫人（尊称）”，我记得的是访客登记簿里登记过的那一声，1970 年记下了，至今仍被说成门厅里最安静的一声。
madam 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，女士是唯一会因为被好好登记而变得更好的女士。
